title: Quantinuum and UWA expand Australia's quantum computing push
excerpt: Quantinuum and UWA partner to expand quantum computing access, develop skills and accelerate applications across key Australian industries.
content:
News | October 6, 2026

By Asma Adhimi



Quantinuum has signed a memorandum of understanding with The University of Western Australia (UWA) to expand access to advanced quantum computing and help develop Australia’s quantum workforce.

The collaboration will give UWA-affiliated researchers, students and entrepreneurs cloud access to Quantinuum’s full-stack quantum platform, including its latest-generation Helios quantum computer, while supporting work that combines quantum computing with AI and high-performance computing (HPC).

Targeting industrial quantum applications

Quantinuum and UWA plan to explore applications in sectors that are strategically important to the Australian economy, including critical minerals, energy, agriculture and healthcare.

The organizations will also investigate the creation of a university-wide quantum computing applications center at UWA. The proposed center would bring together academic, industry and government stakeholders to identify high-value use cases and assess where quantum technology could provide practical benefits.

“Australia has set an ambitious vision for quantum, and it is making meaningful progress toward turning that vision into reality thanks to leadership from institutions like UWA,” said Marvin Lee, Quantinuum’s Singapore-based Country Leader. “Together, we’re bringing our full suite of capabilities, from world-leading hardware and software to application expertise and ecosystem programs, to develop practical quantum applications and hybrid workflows that will prepare Australia for the quantum era and support the nation’s future prosperity.”

Quantinuum experts will work with UWA researchers and industry partners to evaluate potential use cases, establish technical benchmarks and test workflows combining quantum computing, AI and HPC.

Building skills and startup links

The partnership also has a strong workforce-development component. UWA researchers, developers and entrepreneurs will be able to engage with Quantinuum programs including Q-Net and its Startup Partner Program, providing access to training and links to the company’s wider quantum ecosystem.

“Through co-design with potential end users and quantum computing hardware providers, this initiative will create new opportunities for UWA researchers, students and industry partners, while strengthening interdisciplinary collaboration across the University. We look forward to exploring all the opportunities this will bring for our researchers as well as student pathways, internships and workforce training initiatives,” said Professor Jingbo Wang, founder and Director of UWA’s Research Centre for Quantum Information, Simulation and Algorithm.

The agreement reflects a broader push in Australia to turn its research strengths in quantum science into commercial capabilities, skilled jobs and deployable technologies.
